the Web is an important tool in the recruitment and organization of domestic extremist groups.

the Web sites of the domestic extremist groups studied are a valuable source of intelligence for the US government and law enforcement agencies.
the use of semiautomating methodologies to capture and analyze data from the Web is a valuable approach to identifying the structure of domestic extremist groups.
the use of automated methods to analyze extremist Web sites is a promising approach to understanding and monitoring the activities of extremist organizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

semiautomated Web site data capture and organization can be a powerful tool for understanding the nature of domestic extremist and hate group Web sites, and that the resulting data can provide valuable insights into the interorganizational structures of domestic extremist and hat groups.
the Internet is a valuable tool for studying extremist groups and their linkages, and it can also be used to identify and monitor these groups.

semiautomated Web crawling and content extraction can be an effective means of collecting and organizing data on extremist Web sites, but that it is not a panacea and that manual review and analysis of the data are still necessary to fully understand the nature of the threat.

semiautomated methods are useful in the analysis of extremist group linkages and can help analysts understand the structure of these groups and the nature of their relationships.
the Internet provides an excellent platform for analyzing extremist group linkages and content.
automated methods can be used to augment the work of domain experts in identifying the structure and content of the Web.
